newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mostly lower, off lows.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mostly lower, off lows.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly lower, never fully recovering from US trade data early in the session that showed a shrinking overall trade gap.
The US October trade gap narrowed 30.2 percent in October to $7.99 billion, with September revised to $11.44 billion from $11.34 billion.

March yen garnered brief support early from a wider-than-expected gap with Japan, but soon succumbed to an overall strong dollar tone that dragged on continental currencies. The US-Japan gap swelled 30.9 percent to $4.96 billion, the highest since 1995.
Most currencies finished up from their lows, but the tone overall was sluggish, with trade light except for a morning flurry of activity.
March Swiss francs slumped to a fresh contract low in overnight Globex trading, then extended those losses in day trade to post a new low of $0.7515.
One IMM trader said funds were seen buying March Swiss near the lows, helping stem losses.
March marks stumbled to a two-week low, hitting sell-stops in thin trade that extended the move, traders said. Support was pegged at March's contract low of $0.6417 set December 3.

March sterling sank to Monday's session low of $1.6530, but the sell-off stalled there. Traders said $1.6530 acted as a short-term double bottom to halt losses. They said the market had become overvalued and needed to cool off before continuing higher. Several traders noted a "buy-the-dips" sentiment in sterling.
Rallies in U.S. stocks and bonds took center stage late in the day, with action becoming even more thin in currency futures pits, traders said.
"It was really quiet all day and the pits themselves are pretty thin really," an IMM trader said.
"There was some movement but it didn't really follow through, probably because there wasn't any volume to get it going," she said.
Early in the session, the latest weekly jobless claims were reported up to 351,000 in the December 14 week from 350,000 in the prior week.
Third-quarter final U.S. growth will be released on Friday at 0730 CST/1330 GMT. Reuters' survey of economists pegged an average forecast of 2.0 percent growth, unchanged from the previous report.

At settlement, March yen was off $0.000029 to $0.008879, marks ended down $0.0020 to $0.6459, Swiss francs lost $0.0041 to $0.7538, Sterling lost $0.0088 to $1.6616, Canadian dollar rose $0.0002 to $0.7358, Australian dollar rose $0.0028 to $0.7937, and Mexican peso rose $0.000325 to $0.121225.
